Quick notes from SRE/Runtime team after looking at FintechCo's expected QPS and payload sizes:
- With our standard hosted configuration in EU (autoscaled A100-backed pools with T4 fallbacks), realistic sustained commitments we can confidently offer: p50 <= 70 ms, p95 <= 260 ms for text generation endpoints (seq len ~512). These assume the customer's peak QPS per-route doesn't exceed the committed throughput; we should ask FintechCo to include expected per-route QPS in the contract.
- Measurement window: 28-day rolling is fine, but you must define sampling (we recommend continuous daily sampling with 1-minute resolution aggregated into percentiles). Shorter windows (7 days) are stricter and may cause false positives for transient spikes.
- Planned maintenance: excluded if Redwood provides 48-hour notice and the window is <=4 hours per maintenance event; anything longer requires coordination and will be listed as scheduled downtime in the SLA appendix.
- Major incidents: for region-wide failover or operator-driven degradations, we'll use an incident-adjusted window (we tag incident windows and they are not counted against the SLO if the incident is declared and documented).

I'll attach a small trace sample set and a draft clause you can send to legal.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Sarah — attaching the consolidated items we discussed and a single-page commitment matrix below. Please review and let me know if this aligns with FintechCo's procurement needs; if so, we'll incorporate into the master services schedule and circulate for signatures.

Committed latency targets (eu-west-1):
- p50: <= 70 ms (text generation, seq len up to 512)
- p95: <= 260 ms

Measurement & reporting:
- Window: 28-day rolling percentile calculation (continuous sampling at 1-minute granularity, aggregated into daily percentile summaries which are combined into the 28-day window).
- Minimum traffic requirement: measurement applies when average daily QPS across the 28-day window >= 5 RPS for the route being measured. Routes below the minimum default to a baseline monitoring SLA (no financial credit).

Exclusions & exceptions:
- Scheduled maintenance: excluded if Redwood provides >=48 hours' notice; maintenance events excluded <=4 hours per event. More extensive maintenance will be scheduled and communicated and will be listed in the scheduled-downtime appendix.
- Region failovers/incidents: excluded when a formal incident is declared; incidents are documented with timeline and root cause and excluded from SLO calculations.
- Force majeure: standard contract language applies.

Commercials:
- 28-day measurement window is available on enterprise terms with a committed monthly minimum. Tighter p95 targets (below 260 ms) may require reserved capacity and pricing adjustments; see attached pricing-tier-summary.

Attachments: redwood-eu-slo-proposal.pdf, sample-traces-eu-202611.zip, pricing-tier-summary.pdf
